$comment: Kino plugin contract, apiVersion 1 to 14. The single source of truth for every number and rule a plugin meets. The app checks each value against its own code, and a test in the app pins this file to it; sdk/validate.mjs, sdk/run.mjs and the guide's tables read this file. apiVersion 12 (sync providers), 13 and 14 (plugin screens: screen, library, playerPanelTab, playerControl, room, schedule, ai, shared, enhancements) all arrive in Kino 0.9.74, the next release (not published yet); a Kino before 0.9.74 refuses all three.

Alone, with no standalone capability, they get the usual rule. playerControl (Task 8t) is a supplement only beside a panel object (its own player panel, or panel.contributes with playerPanelTab): a standalone set with playerControl and no panel is refused with playerControlNeedsPanelMessage.

The plugin lists and describes titles and plays none: resolve is not required, one of atLeastOneOf is, forbiddenCapabilities and forbiddenFields (streamHosts, and browser only as true: "pages" reads pages for the catalog) are refused. Kino never calls its resolve, never lists it as a source of a title (search, Ver en otros plugins, Buscar dónde verlo, the player's Servidor) and sends its titles to the person's other sources. For Kino 0.9.53 and older also declare and export resolve (throwing not_found) and search or home.

enhancements.$comment: "enhancements": { "<apiVersion>": { "capabilities"?, "screen"?, "settings"?, "panel"? } } (Task 8c; panel, Task 8k). A plugin keeps its own apiVersion, so a Kino older than fromApiVersion (which ignores the unknown key) installs and runs it as before, and lists under the apiVersion that brought them the features only a newer Kino reads. A Kino merges each key it supports (key <= maxApiVersion), in numeric order, over the manifest: capabilities are added, screen, settings and panel replaced, then the whole manifest is validated at that key's apiVersion. A block that fails is dropped and logged (dropped messages, after "enhancements.<key>: "), and an enhancement never refuses the plugin: a key at or below the plugin's apiVersion (notAboveApi), a setting whose type differs from the one the manifest declares (settingRetyped: keep the list a superset of the base one), a screen.replaces the plugin's own apiVersion has no Categorías for (replacesNeedsCategories), and, once the script is probed, exports the block newly needs and the script lacks (missingExports) all drop the block. A key above the Kino's maxApiVersion is ignored silently. The kit's validate reports every drop as a problem. The plugin's apiVersion never moves (its old behaviour stays); only the capabilities listed here gate on the enhancement's apiVersion. A block that adds playerPanelTab must carry the panel with contributes: true, and the other way round (panelTabNeedsPanel). Consent lines of added capabilities (library, playerPanelTab) are asked at install and update like any other; until approved, kino.library calls are refused with permission_denied. Task 18 (G1, apiVersion stays 14): a block may also add schedule (with its jobs, the jobs field: each needs the other, so a block with one and not the other is dropped; a top-level jobs of a manifest whose own apiVersion is below kinoJobs.apiVersion is never read), shared and ai, under exactly the consent of a plain manifest: schedule and ai are red lines asked at install and on the update that adds them, never approved by Kino on its own, unticked in a kit import, revocable in Ajustes; shared is a plain line. Their features gate on the manifest's featureApiVersion, so an older apiVersion plugin runs its jobs, kino.shared and kino.ai on a Kino that read the block, and nowhere else. Task 18 (G13): a block's settings list may not change the sync of a key the manifest (or an earlier block) declares, each list's sync as its own apiVersion reads it (below settings.sync.apiVersion every setting syncs), else the block is dropped (settingResynced): a value would sync on one Kino and stay on the device on another; a new key may say sync false.

dropped.notObject: enhancements: must be an object keyed by apiVersion

dropped.replacesNeedsCategories: "screen.replaces" needs the plugin's categories, which need its own apiVersion to be {min} or more
dropped.badField: "{field}" can't be enhanced (only capabilities, screen, settings, panel and jobs)

goLiveChannel.$comment: Task 11, apiVersion 14: { liveChannel: { provider, code } } tunes to the channel code of the En vivo provider plugin provider. Honoured only for a plugin whose approved contributing panel declares "live" in manifest.panel.contributes.kinds (else dropped, logged needsLiveTabLog), only after the person's own press or submit (fromTriggers, as url and copy), for an installed, usable provider with live channels (never a reservedProviders id; an 18+ provider only while the 18+ code is unlocked). An 18+ channel fails closed through the module's own open (locked: not found). From the player panel while a module channel plays the channel changes in place (the panel and its pin stay); from anywhere else the panel or screen closes and the player opens the channel, as go.play does.

sharedProps.$comment: Task 15 (apiVersion stays 14): properties a whole family of nodes shares, with one meaning everywhere (no component per need). autofocus: on a focusable node (focusableWidgets, or any node with an onTap or onLongPress; never a QR), true; on a render (a tick or an answer) that left focus nowhere or on a node now gone, focus goes to the first such node in tree order; an answer's own focus wins; a node that still holds focus keeps it; on a phone a text field is never autofocused (no keyboard). selected: true or false on a button or a card with an onTap (pressableWidgets): Kino's selected look (filled-tonal; a card: an outline in the primary colour), read as selected; chips and tabs say theirs through value (selected on them is ignored, logged); ui set { key, value: true | false } on such a node sets it and ui toggle { toggle: key, prop: "selected" } flips it, kept until the plugin's next tree. badge: the Badge node's shape, "dot" or { text, textEn?, color? } (text 1 to maxChars, cut beyond; color a colour role, else the default), on a button, a card with an onTap, a tabs node's tab entry and a panel result's tabs entry: a count or a dot on the top end corner (beside a tab's label), read after the node's name. None of the three takes a per-size map. A value on a node that does not take it, or not of its shape, is ignored, logged.

maxWidthFraction.$comment: Task 15: a style property of every node: at most that share of the width its parent offers (the node still wraps its content); with fill it takes exactly that share; placement is the parent's crossAxisAlignment. Off the scale: dropped, logged.

corners.$comment: Task 15: borderRadius also takes a per-corner map of radius tokens; an omitted corner takes the default; start and end follow the reading direction; a key that is no corner is ignored, a value that is no token drops the whole radius, both logged. Fills, clips, outlines and the TV's focus ring follow it.

textTime.$comment: Task 15: a Text's time (epoch ms, a whole number 0 to maxMs) is written by Kino in the app's language: relative (refreshed every refreshMs while shown, no plugin call) or clock (the device's 12/24 h); with a time the text is optional and is a prefix. A bad time is dropped (and the text is then required), logged; a timeFormat without a time is ignored, logged.

enabledAt.$comment: Task 18 (G10, apiVersion stays 14): enabledAt (epoch ms, a whole number 0 to textTime.maxMs; not per size) on a pressable (sharedProps.pressableWidgets: a button, a FloatingActionButton, a card or a ListTile with an onTap; elsewhere ignored, logged): drawn off (no press, no TV focus stop) until that time on the device's clock, then on by itself, with no plugin call (Kino keeps one timer for it while it is drawn). A Text's timeFormat countdown (with a time) writes the wait left until its time, «0:42», «1:02:03» (whole seconds rounded up, at most textTime.maxCountdownMs), rewritten every textTime.countdownRefreshMs while it runs and «0:00» once reached: the «Reenviar en 0:42» beside a button with the same enabledAt. A bad time is ignored, logged.

canRequestFocus.$comment: Task 22 (apiVersion stays 14): canRequestFocus (Flutter's name; true or false, default false; not per size) on any node. On the TV a node that takes no focus of its own (a status Card, a Text, a Row, a Column, a DataTable, a MaterialBanner without an action...) becomes a D-pad stop: Kino's row look while focused (a tonal tint and a 3 dp accent underline, never the white ring), no press (OK does nothing), its content read by a screen reader, in the normal Up/Down/Left/Right traversal and the Scaffold rules. Ignored on a node that already takes focus (an input, a button, a node with an onTap or onLongPress) and on the phone. A non-boolean is ignored, logged. Without it a non-focusable block is read by paging: the TV scrolls a body by 80% of its height before focus moves past what has not shown yet.

listHints.$comment: Task 15: a ListView's newItemsHint: while items are appended (the old last item still in the list) and the person is not at the end, Kino's own chip (its text, never the plugin's) shows over the list's bottom; a tap goes to the end; it hides once the end shows. Only on a list that scrolls itself (one column).

boxProps.$comment: Task 17 (apiVersion stays 14): style properties, every one per size. alignSelf (start, center, end, stretch) places a child of a Row or a Column (or a Card, a Form, a scroll: alignSelfParents) across it, over the parent's crossAxisAlignment; stretch in a row draws as start; elsewhere (a wrapping row's cell too) ignored, logged. textAlign (textAligns) aligns the paragraph of a node that draws text (textAlignWidgets). border { width?, color? } (width 0 to border.maxWidth dp, default border.defaultWidth; color a colour role, else Kino's outline) and background (a colour role: the box's fill, its content in the role's readable on-colour; over color) on a node that draws a box (boxWidgets); elevation 0 to maxElevation, a whole number (Kino's shadow, a card's tonal lift too) on elevationWidgets. minWidth, maxWidth, maxHeight take the size scale beside minHeight; a min above its max drops the max. A value off its scale or shape is dropped, a number out of range clamped, a property on a node that does not take it ignored; all logged.

positioned.$comment: Task 17: a style property (per size) of a child of a Stack (box) only, Flutter's Positioned: any of keys, each a number of dp (0 to maxDp, clamped) or a share of the stack written "25%" (percentPattern, 0 to 100, clamped); a value that is neither drops that key, an unknown key is ignored, both sides and a size on one axis ignore the size; all logged. Unpositioned children keep the stack's alignment and size it; a stack whose children are all positioned takes its own width (the width offered) and its height/minHeight (else 0). Children are drawn and focused in their order, clipped to the stack, sized and placed inside it (never pressed outside).

motion.$comment: Task 17: opacity (a style property, per size, every node): 0 to 1, clamped; below minInteractiveOpacity the node takes no press and no focus (Kino treats it as off). visible: false (not per size) hides a node as hidden: true does. animate (a style property, per size) on a box (boxProps.boxWidgets) or a positioned child, elsewhere ignored: { duration?, curve? }, duration whole ms minMs to maxMs (clamped; default defaultMs), curve one of curves (else the first): changes of its size, opacity, fill, place (positioned) and visibility between renders glide (AnimatedContainer, AnimatedOpacity and AnimatedSwitcher in one property). The device's animations off (animator duration scale 0) turns them off; an animation never delays a press or focus (a node gliding out takes neither); at most maxAnimated animating nodes per screen, the rest drop their animate (logged once). All other problems logged.

tooltip.$comment: Task 17: tooltip (and tooltipEn; not per size) on a node that does something (sharedProps.focusableWidgets, or any node with an onTap or onLongPress; never a QR), elsewhere ignored, logged: at most maxChars characters (cut beyond, logged). Kino draws it: on a phone on a long press (a node with its own onLongPress shows none: its action wins), on a TV after tvDelayMs of focus (hidden when focus leaves), shown showMs; a screen reader gets it as the long-press action's label. Never essential information: a person who never sees it misses nothing. A disabled node shows the plugin's own tooltip too (Kino adds none of its own).

flutterNodes.$comment: Task 17: Flutter's own nodes under their Flutter names (the older names are fab, listTile, avatar, pageView). FloatingActionButton { icon (required), labelText? (the extended form; else what a screen reader says: the tooltip, else Kino's own word), onPressed (required), fabPosition end | center (per size) }: Kino draws it over the bottom of the plugin's area (a player panel's body), never in place, never under the system bars or the keyboard; at most maxFabs per screen, never inside a list, a table, a pop-up, a ListTile or an image's fallback (dropped, logged); it takes selected, badge, autofocus and tooltip; on a TV a focus stop with the ring. ListTile { title (required), subtitle?, leading?, trailing? (one node each of tileSlotWidgets, else dropped; never pressed themselves), dense (per size) }: Material's heights, the whole tile one press and one TV stop (ring only with an onTap); selected (with an onTap) fills it with primaryContainer. CircleAvatar { image? (https, Kino's image pipeline; a failed one shows the initials), text? (initials, at most avatarMaxTextChars, cut), icon?, radius (dp, avatarMinRadius to avatarMaxRadius, clamped; default avatarDefaultRadius; per size), backgroundColor? (a colour role, default primaryContainer), labelText? (what a screen reader says) }: always a circle (no borderRadius). PageView { children (the pages, at most maxPages), initialPage (the first look only, clamped to the last page, logged), onPageChanged (its event's value: the settled page's index), autoPlayMs? (autoPlayMinMs to autoPlayMaxMs, raised or lowered, logged; paused while touched or focused and with animations off), viewportFraction (viewportFractionMin to 1, clamped; below 1 Kino's carousel: the neighbours peek), padEnds (default true) }: swiped on a phone, Left and Right at a page's edge on a TV (a page with nothing focusable leaves the pager itself as the stop), Kino's page dots under it, its place read by a screen reader; never inside a sideways scroll or a table cell (dropped, logged).

scaffold.$comment: Task 17 item G: Scaffold { appBar?, body (required), floatingActionButton?, bottomNavigationBar? } only as the root of a screen result (a screen's or a player panel's root; anywhere else, or in an answer's pop-up, dropped, logged), read slot by slot (slotTypes: the node each holds; body any node); a result whose root is a Scaffold is drawn in layout fill (a layout given other than fill is ignored, logged). Its AppBar is pinned at the top of the plugin's area, BELOW Kino's own title bar (the plugin's name and Close, always drawn by Kino, never replaced or covered); its body takes the bounded height left (a ListView or a scroll in it scrolls itself, the bars stay; the keyboard shrinks the body); its FloatingActionButton (or one in the body) sits above its NavigationBar. AppBar { title? (a string, read as a heading for a screen reader, with its titleEn twin; or, Flutter's way, any node: a TabBar, a Row of buttons, an Image..., read as any child, at most maxAppBarTitleNodes nodes, else dropped, logged; it takes the room left of the actions, a TabBar there scrolls sideways, a Text node is the heading; on the TV its focusables are part of the row, Left/Right across them then to the actions), leading? (an IconButton), actions? (at most maxAppBarActions IconButtons, the rest dropped, logged; each needs a labelText), bottom? (a TabBar), centerTitle, backgroundColor? (a colour role), elevation }: only a Scaffold's appBar; appBarDp tall, appBarPanelDp in a player panel. NavigationBar { items: [{ key, icon, label, labelEn?, badge? }] (minNavItems to maxNavItems, the rest dropped; fewer drops the bar; logged), value (an item's key) or selectedIndex, onChanged (its event's value: the item's key; not in state.inputs) }: only a Scaffold's bottomNavigationBar; Material's bar on a phone, a bottom row of focusable items with Kino's ring on a TV. TV D-pad: the AppBar's leading and actions, the body, the bottom bar, the button (Compose's geometry; Up from the body's first stop reaches the bar); Back closes or pops as everywhere.

fallbackWidgets.$comment: Task 7i-1, apiVersion 14: an image's fallback is one node drawn in the image's box when the picture fails or there is no url (with a fallback an image whose url is missing or not one Kino may load is kept); at any depth in it only these widgets, and no onTap or onLongPress (ignored, logged). A card's flush (a layout prop) drops its own padding and clips its children to its shape. A wrapping row's cells stretch to their line's height unless the row's align is start, center or end.

declaredPopups.$comment: Task 7i-2, apiVersion 14: an answer's ui is a list of the same ui operations as a node's action (at most maxUiOps), run as the answer is applied; the deferredOps among them wait for the tree the answer's state change asks for (when it asks for one) and run on it, so a declared pop-up opens with its new body, never the last one's; a timer's answer drops ui, logged; Back before that tree arrives cancels them. A popup node's onClose (an event name with the node's arg, or { ui?, event?, arg? }) runs after the person dismissed that open pop-up (Back, Kino's close, a tap outside): its ui operations, then its event; never when a pop-up button, a menu item, an answer's ui or a new pop-up closed it; a go and any dismissDroppedOps in it are dropped, logged. Back always closes: the onClose event is no press (no kino.qr.scan, no go.titleByIds) and its answer drops dismissDroppedFields and the dismissDroppedOps of its ui, logged. The deferredOps also wait for a route the answer moves; only the newest held one is kept; a newer pop-up, a failed or invalid render, Try again and the error state drop them. A blank title is no title: no empty row is drawn, Kino's close (an X alone, Task 7k) starts the bottom row and the pop-up's own buttons sit together at its end; with a title the X ends the title's row.

anchor.$comment: Task 15: a popup node's anchor (a node's key): drawn next to that node (above it when there is more room above, else below), sized to its content and at most the area's width, over the content with no scrim, taking no layout space; ui open and close, Back and a tap outside work as for any pop-up; it has no close button of its own; TV focus goes into it and stays there, and Back gives it back to the anchor. Without an anchor, or when the anchor is not on screen or there is no room above or below it, the kind's own placement (logged once). A screen-format player panel draws a popup only with an anchor.
anchor.notOnScreenLog: screen: popup anchor "<key>" is not on screen, the pop-up drawn in its own place
anchor.misfitLog: screen: popup anchor has too little room above and below it for the pop-up, drawn in its own place

pressBudget.$comment: Task 18 (G6, G7, apiVersion stays 14): an action object may carry timeoutMs, its event's own call budget: a whole number of ms from minActionTimeoutMs to maxActionTimeoutMs (clamped, logged; not a number, ignored, logged), only on a press (pressFields: a button's onPressed is its onTap; elsewhere, or without an event, ignored, logged) and honoured only when the person's own press or submit sends it (a change, a tick, open or a load-more keep limits.callTimeoutMs). Kino's pending cue: while the call of a press runs past pendingCueMs, the node pressed (a button, a FloatingActionButton, a card or a ListTile with an onTap) is drawn in Kino's busy look until its answer (or its failure). loadingField (loading: true or false, not per size) on such a pressable draws the same look from your tree: Kino's spinner in place of a button's icon (a ListTile's trailing), no press (a TV keeps its focus there), read as busy (busyWord); elsewhere ignored, logged.

forceError.$comment: Task 18 (G8, apiVersion stays 14): Flutter's forceErrorText (and forceErrorTextEn; not per size) on any input: the plugin's own verdict (a server's code refused, an address already taken), drawn under the field exactly as a failed form check's error (the error role, read with the field by a screen reader), a failed submit's own error winning while it shows. The person's edit of that field (a change, ui set or clear) hides it until the plugin's next verdict: the answer to the person's next press or submit, or a different text, shows it again. At most maxChars characters (cut, logged); not a text, ignored, logged. It never blocks a submit (only Kino's own rules do).

settingsAutoSave.$comment: Task 18 (G11, G12, apiVersion stays 14): a settings node's autoSave: true (else false; not a boolean, ignored, logged) saves its toggle and select settings (types) as the person changes them, through the screen's own write (the same store and sync; your validateSettings is not asked, as for bind; toggles and selects keep your web session); a refused write puts the stored value back with Kino's generic line. A setting with unlockWith changes (and so saves) only after its code in the form's own prompt. When every valued setting the node shows saves this way the form draws no Guardar nor Descartar; a text, url, password or list it shows keeps them. Without autoSave every change waits for Guardar, as in Ajustes. G12: a settings node whose keys hold no valued setting (only action, status, section, link, help or qr items, e.g. keys: ["logout"]) draws those items and no Guardar nor Descartar: an action runs from its own button (its confirm first), as in Ajustes.

colorHints.$comment: Screen asks (#8): a colour that is no role logs its closest role: a role in another case, or one of these words (success and info are banner and toast roles, never a node's color).

screenAsks.$comment: Screen asks (apiVersion 14, not shipped yet: additive inside 14). (1) An answer's config may write or empty a password setting: kept exactly as given (never trimmed; blank empties it; required ones are never emptied; at most the type's maxChars), saved through the same store, sync namespace and sync record as Ajustes' save (a synced password reaches the person's other devices, an emptied one is cleared there too; a device-only one, "sync": false, stays on the device), never read back by a screen, never in a log line (only its key). (2) A textInput with secret: true (Flutter's obscureText) is drawn masked on phone and TV; its text lives only in Kino's memory, never in the state, a render, a change or a tick: it goes only with the person's own tap or submit (state.inputs.<key>, and a form's or the field's own submit value), and is cleared once that call ends unless the answer gives one back in state.inputs.<key>. Its value from the tree and its onChange are ignored, logged; secret on a multi-line field, or a secret that is not true or false, drops the field. Bound (bind) only to a password setting (secretBindHolds), written on commit when not empty; a password is bound only by a secret field. (3) A settings node's onSaved (event name or { event, arg }) is sent after Kino's form in it saved (its Guardar, or with autoSave a toggle or select that saved on change and changed something: kind save with that key) or an action button in it finished, with value { kind: save | action, ok, keys, action?, reason? } (setting keys only, never values), as a change: not a press, never coalesced with ticks, which wait behind it; a save or action that ends after the screen closed sends nothing.

qr.$comment: (4) A QrImage's countdown: expiresInMs (minExpiryMs..maxExpiryMs, counted from when Kino first draws that value) or expiresAt (epoch ms, read against the device's clock once, at most maxExpiryMs away; both given: expiresAt ignored). Kino draws a bar and the seconds left under the code, ticked by itself every tickMs between your calls, and once it reaches zero the code dims under its own 'expired' text. A countdown keeps its deadline while the value stays the same (re-sending expiresInMs never restarts it; a different expiresAt does); a new value starts a new one. onExpire (an event name or { event, arg }) is sent ONCE per value, value { phase, remainingMs }: phase renew renewBeforeMs before the end when given (bounded like expiresInMs; not below the lifetime: half of it used, logged), else expired at zero; never while the screen is hidden (one that came due goes once it shows again, expired if the end passed too), never for a withheld code (it holds one of your secrets), never twice (a slow or missing answer leaves the old code counting down to its expired look; your every timer is the fallback). It is nobody's press: its answer keeps what a timer's keeps (state, toast, close, config). onExpire and renewBeforeMs need an expiry; renewBeforeMs needs onExpire; else ignored, logged.

steps.$comment: (5) steps: a setup flow in Kino's own look, for any plugin (never Flutter's Stepper name, which reads as the number stepper). items [{ key, title, titleEn?, subtitle?, subtitleEn?, state, children? }], 1 to maxSteps (key valid and distinct, title required): done (collapsed to its subtitle, else Kino's Done), current (open: its children drawn under it) or pending (collapsed, dimmed). Exactly one current: none while a step is still to do makes the first one not done current; several keep the first, the others pending; an unknown state reads as pending; all logged. Only the current step's children are read (one level below the node, each header one node of the budget). onStepTapField (an event name or { event }): a done step is pressable (touch, or OK with the TV's focus ring) and sends it with the step's key as arg; without it nothing is pressable and focus goes from above straight into the current step. A screen reader reads each header as Step i of n: title, state.

layout.$comment: Task 14 (apiVersion 14, no new apiVersion): a screen result's layout, chosen per result: on a screen() answer's root object (beside every; a deeper node's is not read), on a screen-format panel() result beside root (a panel root's own layout is ignored, logged). scroll (the default; absent or null): a player panel's body scrolls and the tree has no height limit (a list draws flat, flex does nothing), exactly as before. fill: the root is drawn at the panel body's bounded size, with no body scroll; flex shares the height left and a list with it is lazy and scrolls itself (TV: Up/Down pages it, the Task 7k rule). A render whose fixed (non-flex) children of the root alone reach the body's bottom is drawn in the scroll layout instead, logged once per screen (fallbackLog); it tries fill again with a new size, layout or set of root children. The dock and the drawer end above the keyboard, so a bottom row stays above it. A full screen's root is always the screen's bounded area (what fill does), whatever layout says. Any other value is logged and read as scroll. ListView stickToBottom (layoutProps.list, responsive): a lazy single-column list opens at its last item, follows new items while the person is at its end or one item from it, stays put once they scroll up and sticks again when they come back to the end; Kino keeps that per list key while the list is drawn (a re-render keeps it; a new key or a closed screen starts over). In a flat list (scroll layout, inside a scroll) it does nothing, logged once per screen (stickFlatLog).
layout.fallbackLog: screen: layout fill does not fit, using scroll
layout.stickFlatLog: screen: list stickToBottom works only in a list that scrolls itself (layout fill, or a full screen), ignored in a flat list

aliases.$comment: Task 8e: the Flutter-style names are the documented spelling of a node's type and properties; the older names above (widgets, styleProps, ...) are what Kino reads internally and stay accepted as aliases. Kino (PluginScreenOutput via ScreenNames) and the kit rewrite every node object at the one point it is read, before validation: a type of types becomes its older name (a TextField with multiline true or a maxLines above 1 in any size class becomes textArea, its multiline and maxLines dropped); a type of implied also sets that property (a different value given is logged and replaced); each props pair moves the canonical value under the older name (when both are given the canonical one wins and the clash is logged; a canonical null counts as absent); buttonProps only on a button (elsewhere logged and ignored); a table's columns take columnProps and its rows and cells are rewritten too. Anything else (an unknown name such as Stepper) is read as before: an unknown type is dropped and logged. Log lines name the older spelling. names: every type name the docs list (kino.screen.names).

extraIcons.$comment: Task 8v: the larger icon set (Material Symbols, outlined, as Kino already ships them). icons is every name; these names are read from apiVersion on; below it such a name is an unknown one (panel.icon draws defaultIcon). The screen surface (screen.icon, a tree's Icon, button, menu item and empty and error states, a panel in screen mode) exists only from apiVersion 14, so there every name of icons is known.

contributes.$comment: Task 8k, apiVersion 14: "panel": { "contributes": true, "label"?, "labelEn"?, "icon"? | "iconFile"? } with the capability playerPanelTab (each needs the other; a missing label is the plugin's name, cut to labelMaxChars). The player panel is a tab host: one outer tab per source. With a contributed tab the bar is drawn and Kino's own information panel is first (fixed), then the panel of the plugin that provides the stream (its own tabs kept inside it), then the contributed ones in the person's order (Ajustes, Paneles del reproductor; default install order), at most maxTabs; with no contribution the drawer is as before (a plugin's own panel replaces Kino's, no bar). Each outer tab is labelled with the plugin's name (a name that reads like Kino is shown qualified, as "Plugin «<name>»") and its icon (never Kino's info icon), never the panel's own title; the id kino is reserved. A contributed panel(context) / panelAction / playerEvent is the same contract (legacy or screen format) for a plugin's title (never an 18+ one, never a title of an 18+ plugin; an 18+ plugin's tab only while the 18+ code is unlocked; not for M3U lists, own channels or other non-plugin content), with a context built from an allow-list (contextFields, player.playerFields): context.ref is an opaque id (foreignRefPrefix + foreignRefHexChars hex characters of foreignRefMac keyed by the install's own random salt over foreignRefInput: the same title gives this plugin the same id on that install, another plugin or install another one; opaque, not secret), contextAdds (foreign: true and source: { pluginId, name } of the plugin that provides the stream), notSent never sent (the owner's copy and its autoNext, which names a ref of the owner). It is called only while its tab is the selected one and the drawer is open (refreshMs only then), and playerEvent reaches it only then too (from the moment its tab opens until it closes, the drawer closes or the title ends), while approved and switched on (copyChanged without its label). Its player actions are honoured only in the answer to a panelAction whose trigger is in playerActionsFrom, and only playerActionKept (a seek of the title playing); with the playerControl capability (kinoPlayerControl, Task 8j) from any origin, and playerActionKeptWithControl; every other player field belongs to the playing plugin and is dropped. Its go never opens a plugin's title (goDropped). Consent: playerPanelTab is approved by the person with consentLine (red), never auto-approved, revocable with the per-plugin switch switchLabel (the person's, synced).

kinds.$comment: Task 11, apiVersion 14: which content the contributed tab joins: "title" (a plugin's title, the 8k rule) and "live" (an En vivo module channel, kinoLivePanel). Optional; a non-empty list of values (duplicates kept once); an unknown value, an empty list or a non-list is an invalid manifest (badMessage); only beside contributes: true (needsContributesMessage).

sync.$comment: apiVersion 12, only with the syncProvider capability, which requires it: a syncProvider plugin without a sync block or without keySecret is refused (keySecret.missingMessage). keySecret names one of the plugin's own password settings: Kino, host side, derives the sync key from that setting's value as the plugin's runtime reads it (the profile in use) (HKDF-SHA256, salt = saltPrefix + pluginId + ":" + accountId, where accountId is the pluginId too), so the key never travels and a second device needs only the provider's own settings. The derivation is public and the plugin reads that setting, so the plugin and its service CAN read the synced data (the consent line consentLine, always in red); it must be a high-entropy token, never a password a person picks (offline guessing from any blob). There is no random-key mode: such a key could never reach a second device.
sync.badMessage: The "sync" field must be an object with an optional "mode" of "poll" or "realtime" and optional positive whole numbers "pullEveryMs", "pushDebounceMs" and "maxBlobBytes" (at most 4194304)
sync.consentLine: Sincronizará tus datos a través de su servicio: el plugin y su servicio podrán leerlos

keySecret.missingMessage: The "syncProvider" capability needs a "sync" field whose "keySecret" is the key of one of the plugin's own "password" settings
keySecret.badMessage: The "keySecret" of the "sync" field must be the key of one of the plugin's own "password" settings
keySecret.noDefaultMessage: The setting the "keySecret" of the "sync" field names must not have a "default"
keySecret.deviceOnlyMessage: The "keySecret" of the "sync" field can't name a setting with "sync": false

generateKey.$comment: apiVersion 13, optional, default false (below 13 the key is ignored): Kino makes the keySecret value itself, keyBytes random bytes from a SecureRandom as lower-case hex (64 characters), only while that setting is empty, at two moments: when the person switches the provider on and when they press Enviar configuración (before the values are read, so an empty key never hides that button). Saved through the settings form's own save, sealed exactly like a typed password, never logged and never drawn in the form on any device (its value is kept and saved back). Never replaces a value that exists; a value received from another device always replaces a generated one.
generateKey.badMessage: The "generateKey" of the "sync" field must be true or false

provision.$comment: The keys of the plugin's own settings (secret or not) a pairing hands to another device so it can run the same provider; it must include keySecret, so it is always there. The receiving device saves them like typed values but does not run the plugin's validateSettings on them (as for action.setSettings). From apiVersion 13 it may name a device-only password (settings.sync false) for a one-shot secret such as a 2FA password: the sender sends it only while it holds a value (blank, it is left out and never blocks the send) and adds a plain line naming its label; the receiver lists its label only and stores it sealed and device-only exactly as a typed one (never synced, never in a backup); the plugin clears it itself (an action's clearSettings) once used. keySecret is never a device-only password (keySecret.deviceOnlyMessage).
provision.badMessage: The "provision" of the "sync" field must be a list of at most 8 different keys of the plugin's own settings that hold a value
provision.needsKeySecretMessage: The "provision" of the "sync" field must include its "keySecret"
provision.deviceOnlyTextMessage: The "provision" of the "sync" field can't name a text setting with "sync": false

english.$comment: Kino 0.9.55, apiVersion 9 (below it, and on an older Kino, the keys are unknown and ignored, never checked): the English variant of a setting's label, hint and confirm, of an option's and a list field's texts, and of section.label. Same limits as the base field (confirmEn only where confirm is, and only with it). The base text is the Spanish default and the fallback; Kino shows the variant when it speaks English. Other languages: unknown keys, ignored.

sync.$comment: apiVersion 13, a password or a text setting only: "sync": false keeps its value on the device where it was typed (a 2FA password the plugin clears once used; a phone number shown as typed). Never sealed to a paired device, never set or cleared by a value another device sends, never in a backup or a kit; the plugin reads it and may clear it. A password one may still be named in a sync provision (a one-shot secret, stored device-only on the receiver too); a text one never (manifest.sync.provision.deviceOnlyTextMessage). A text keeps drawing as a text field: nothing is masked. Default true: the value syncs as always. Below apiVersion 13 the key is unknown, so ignored.
sync.onlyPasswordOrTextMessage: Only a setting of type password or text has "sync" ("{key}")
sync.notBooleanMessage: "sync" of the setting "{key}" must be true or false

unlockWith.$comment: apiVersion 14, a toggle or a select setting only: "unlockWith": "adultCode" makes Kino ask the device's 18+ code (its own prompt, phone and TV; the default code is announced while it rules) before the person moves the setting AWAY from its default (a toggle off its default, a select to any other option) in Kino's settings form: Ajustes ▸ the plugin's tab and a screen's or a panel's settings node. Back toward the default never asks. The change applies only once the code is accepted; a wrong code or Cancelar leaves the old value; the plugin never sees the code and nothing else is unlocked. The value syncs as any other setting; the code is asked per device at the moment of the change. A plugin's own writes may only move it toward its default: an answer's config away from it is refused (screen.lockedWhy), an action's setSettings is refused whole, and a field may never be bound to it (screen.lockedBind): show it in a settings node. One value for now (values); others may come. Below apiVersion 14 the key is unknown, so ignored.
unlockWith.onlyToggleOrSelectMessage: Only a setting of type toggle or select has "unlockWith" ("{key}")
unlockWith.badValueMessage: "unlockWith" of the setting "{key}" must be one of: {values}
unlockWith.lockedWhy: is locked (unlockWith {value}): only the person moves it away from its default, in Kino's settings form
unlockWith.lockedBind: bind "{key}" is locked (unlockWith {value}): show it in a settings node

linkOnly.$comment: apiVersion 12 (additive): an action with "linkOnly": true is never drawn on any device; it runs only as the confirm target of another action's link (action.link), after Kino's own question. For a two-step link (find, then confirm) the person then sees one button.
linkOnly.onlyActionMessage: Only a setting of type action has "linkOnly" ("{key}")
linkOnly.notBooleanMessage: "linkOnly" of the setting "{key}" must be true or false

devices.$comment: apiVersion 12 (additive): any settings item may say which devices draw it, "devices": ["phone"] / ["tv"] / both; absent = every device. Host side only: on a device it leaves out, the item is not drawn nor checked by the form, but its value is still stored, saved back unchanged, synced, provisioned and read by the plugin (kino.config). Below apiVersion 12 the key is ignored. The Node kit renders no form, so it only validates the field.
devices.badMessage: "devices" of the setting "{key}" must be a list of different devices: "phone", "tv"

configAids.$comment: apiVersion 12 configuration aids in the settings form. link: { key, type: "link", label (+labelEn), url, hint? }: a button that opens url through the system only when the person taps it (https only, no user info, at most linkUrlMaxChars), with Kino's "Abrir enlace" and the host under it; on TV the address as text plus a QR. Kino makes no request to that host and it is no network access of the plugin's; an address holding one of the plugin's secrets is not shown. help: { key, type: "help", label? (+labelEn; default Kino's "Ayuda"), title? (+titleEn, at most helpTitleMaxChars), body (+bodyEn, at most helpBodyMaxChars; one of them required) }: a button that opens a modal titled with the plugin's name, plain text only (newlines kept, no markup, nothing clickable), scrubbed of the plugin's secrets; a missing base or English text falls back to the other. Their label, title and body may hold no control character (a body keeps its line breaks), invisible formatting or direction override. Kino opens a link's canonical address, the one whose host it shows. At most maxLinks links and maxHelps helps; they count among the sections, statuses and actions.

statusHide.$comment: apiVersion 13 (of the settings list in effect: an enhancements block's key when the block replaced settings, else the plugin's own, G5), additive: a settingsStatus() answer may carry hide: [setting keys]; the settings form (phone and TV) does not draw those items while that answer is current (a failed answer hides nothing). Their stored values stay, nothing is deleted, and they still count for the form's own rules; unknown keys and non-strings are ignored, entries past maxEntries are never read. A qr setting with no text draws nothing at all.

setSettings.$comment: Additive action.setSettings (no apiVersion): an action may answer setSettings: { <key>: <string> } to fill the plugin's own text or select settings and, from passwordApiVersion (13, of the settings list in effect: an enhancements block's key when the block replaced settings, else the plugin's own, G5), its password settings (never a url: its value would become a server the plugin may reach, and only the person types one; never a toggle, list or valueless one). A password filled this way (a "Create key" action writing random bytes) is saved and sealed exactly like a typed one (a "sync": false one stays on the device), is never logged, and every password value the answer names is scrubbed from the action's own message and link, so it is never shown back. Only an action the person ran fills anything: a settingsStatus answer's setSettings is ignored. Kino does not run the plugin's validateSettings on them. Each value is trimmed and checked like a typed one; a required setting is never emptied; a key also in clearSettings, a value holding one of the plugin's secrets, a non-string, an unknown key or more than maxEntries keys refuse the whole field (nothing applied, Kino's generic error, the message still shows). Kino saves the values through the settings form's own save, so they reach the person's other devices and the profile in use like typed ones. Only from the plugin's own settings form.

link.$comment: Additive action.link (no apiVersion): an action may answer link: { candidate, confirm }. Kino shows its own question ("Is this you, <candidate>?") with Confirm and Cancel; Cancel runs nothing, Confirm runs the confirm action once. candidate: a string, 1 to candidateMaxChars after trimming, no control or invisible formatting characters, scrubbed like any plugin text, shown as plain text. Runs of spaces collapse to one; any space but the ASCII one and the fillers that draw nothing (U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800) refuse it. The question names the asking plugin by its manifest name. confirm: the key of ANOTHER action setting of the same plugin that declares no confirm/confirmEn question of its own. Anything else refuses the link: the action's own message is still shown, with Kino's generic error. A link in the confirm action's own answer is ignored (no chains); one pending link at a time, a newer one replaces it, leaving the form drops it.

loadingElement.$comment: Kino 0.9.64, additive (no apiVersion): { type: "loading", text?, textEn? } draws a spinner with the text (else Kino's «Cargando…»). Answer at once with the tab's shell plus a loading element and a refreshMs, and the next call fills it in. From Kino 0.9.64 the panel context carries features: ["loading"]; an older Kino sends no features and drops the element as an unknown type, so check context.features and answer a status line there instead.

screen.$comment: Task 8i, opt-in per result: panel(context) may return { format: "screen", root, title?, titleEn?, tabs?, tab?, refreshMs?, accent?, layout? } (apiVersion 14; below it, or an unknown format, the result is read as the legacy panel, logged). root is a tree of the screen nodes, read like screen() with these limits; the drawer keeps its title, tabs, refreshMs (THE periodic call; no every in a panel) and accent. In screen mode the context gains state (Kino's, kept for the title's playback) and size (the drawer's size classes); panelAction gets { event: { key?, trigger, name, arg?, value?, values }, context } and its answer honours answerFields; droppedAnswerFields and legacyAnswerFields are dropped, logged. With plugin screens switched off a screen-format result shows no panel; legacy panels keep working: context.features carries contextFeature only while they are on, so the plugin can answer a legacy panel then. A playerEvent answer's panel (either format) shows in the open panel only for apiVersion 14 plugins (below it, ignored as before); its state is never applied.

maxBytes.$comment: Task 7i-1: kino.fetch option maxBytes, from apiVersion 14 (below it the option is unknown and ignored): the body is read up to that many bytes and the read stops there (decoded bytes, after the transport's decompression; a cut text may end inside a character), except in a runtime holding sealed values (secrets, Kino's TMDB key), where the body is read whole up to maxBodyBytes (over it too_large), redacted whole and only then cut; the answer then has truncated: true (false when the whole body fit). Out of range or not a whole number: invalid_request. Never past the call's own response cap.

stopAt.$comment: Task 8u: kino.fetch option stopAt, from apiVersion 14 (below it ignored like any unknown option): a marker of 1 to maxChars printable ASCII characters (0x20-0x7E); the read ends as soon as the decoded text holds it, ASCII case-insensitive, keeping everything up to and including it, with truncated: true when more followed. Text responses only: a byte answer fails with invalid_request (notText). With maxBytes, whichever comes first; never past the call's response cap. In a charset whose ASCII bytes are not those characters (UTF-16, UTF-32, a stateful one) the body is read as without stopAt and the decoded text is cut. In a runtime holding sealed values the body is read whole, redacted, then cut at the marker (searched in the redacted text) and at maxBytes.

syncCall.$comment: A syncProvider's syncPull and syncPush calls (only those, only while Kino runs them) may move the blob the manifest declares: each kino.fetch request (its JSON, the base64 body included) and each response body may reach ceil(sync.maxBlobBytes * 4/3) + envelopeChars, and so may the call's answer, instead of maxRequestChars, maxBodyBytes and runtime.maxResultChars. Hosts, quotas, redirects and timeouts are unchanged. Kino 0.9.74.

anyHost.$comment: A host reached ONLY through an approved fetchHosts "any" (not declared, not a typed server): https on port 443, a public IPv4 literal or a dotted public name (a single-label name such as router is refused), on every redirect hop and for the hidden page's start address too. Each such request spends a budget on top of maxRequestsPerCall: perSite in perSiteWindowMs (a site is the registrable domain, so its subdomains count together) and perPlugin in perPluginWindowMs, refilled continuously and kept per plugin for the whole app (a runtime that closes and reopens keeps it). nuvioPerSite/nuvioPerPlugin: a converted Nuvio scraper's, scaled with its larger per-call cap. Over budget the request fails with errorCode, never queued. Declared hosts (insecureHttp ones included) and typed servers keep their own rules and never spend it. The hidden page (kino.browser) under the grant: its start address and every later top-level navigation of a capture (always for a CloudStream page) follow one rule: a declared or typed host by its own rules, any other host https on port 443 at a dotted public name (not limited to the plugin's hosts); on the proxy path a main-frame server redirect target may be contacted once before the capture ends blocked (detection, not prevention); subresources stay any public host (never the LAN) and spend no budget. From Kino 0.9.55.

browser.onlyWhen: the person pressed play, or a download the person started (never a background resolve such as the live zap's resolve ahead, which Kino skips for a browser plugin); a download's capture never waits for another page: busy at once

captureAll.options: captureAll (every matching request until the page settles), alsoMatch (more patterns, only with captureAll), waitForCookie (a cookie the page must also hold; alone: a cookie-only page with no match), returnCookiesOnTimeout (a timeout answers what the page had, with timedOut, instead of the timeout error)
captureAll.rules: match and alsoMatch are searched anywhere in each URL, case-insensitively unless the pattern starts with (?-i); requests are deduplicated by URL, the primary match (the first request matching match) first; with waitForCookie the page never autoplays and the settle starts once both the match and the cookie hold; captureAll with waitForCookie needs a match; the answer adds its keys only when one of these options was used

page.onlyWhen: the person is using the app: their own search, Home, list, title or play (a resolve also for a download they started); never a background call (prewarm, the live zap's resolve ahead, sync, update checks), and a list's read only with the app in front. Never clicks, taps, types or scrolls: only a check that completes with no input passes
page.topLevel: every top-level navigation and the document read stay on the plugin's kino.fetch hosts (https); else blocked, no HTML

tracking.consentLineNoHosts: Le contará al servidor que escribas en su configuración qué ves y cuándo lo terminas

kinoDevice.$comment: kino.device (Kino 0.9.55, every apiVersion): the UI Kino shows on this device, "tv" or "phone" (a tablet gets whatever Kino shows it, usually "phone"). Undefined on an older Kino. The Node kit says "phone" unless run.mjs gets --device tv or the environment has KINO_DEVICE=tv.

kinoSeed.$comment: kino.seed(session) (Kino 0.9.55, every apiVersion): a plugin shares ONE anonymous, free guest session of its source so people in regions that cannot log in have live sessions to seed from. Best-effort and synchronous: it answers nothing and never throws into the plugin. Kino keeps only the allowed keys (each a short string or a finite number), drops the whole thing unless the three required ones are present and non-blank, and sends it to Kino's error board only when the plugin's telemetry consent is on. Absent on an older Kino: feature-detect with typeof kino.seed === "function". The Node kit has it, sends nothing and logs which keys Kino would keep.

byTitle.$comment: Kino 0.9.55, apiVersion 9 (below it the prelude drops title and year, so the query needs ids; kino.meta.byTitle is absent): kino.meta({ type, title, year? }) instead of ids (ids win when both come). Kino searches TMDB (type's endpoint, es-MX, first page) and keeps a hit whose es-MX or original title equals the asked one once both are normalised (lowercase, no accents, punctuation as spaces); with a year, that exact year wins, else one within yearSlack. A tie (same title and year, or same title and no year) or no match answers null, never a guess. Then the answer is the ids lookup's, same shape, cache (keyed by type, normalised title and year), budget and timeout. year without title, a bad title or a bad year: invalid_request.

kinoNuvio.comment: Experiment (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-kino-nuvio-design.md): the plugin names its Nuvio repos (nuvioRepos); the app installs the scrapers it asks for exactly as the importer does (no screen) and the plugin asks them for streams. Nothing new runs: every scraper keeps the importer's hosts, torrent filter, request budget and 75 s resolve.

consentLine.en: Installs and uses Nuvio scrapers from the repository it names to look for links

cacheTtlByRouteMs.$comment: KinoTmdbTtl.forPath: tv = a series by id, its seasons and episodes; stable = a movie, person or collection by id, any title's credits, images and the like, /find, /genre, /configuration; search = /search; lists = /trending, /discover and the lists; anything else, an empty answer or a 404: cacheTtlMs.

kinoTmdb.$keyOrder: Kino's own key first, behind its cache, in-flight dedup and the two kinoKey limits; the person's key (their Ajustes setting, else a Stremio addon's they agreed to) only when Kino's key gets one of personKeyOn; with neither, a cached copy up to staleMaxDays old, else rate_limited (unavailable when TMDB refused Kino's key). no_tmdb_key only on a build without a key of Kino's and a person without one. A key a plugin keeps in its own settings is never read.

kinoLibrary.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "library" (Task 8b): kino.library.watched({ limit?, kind?, sinceMs? }) and kino.library.saved({ limit?, kind? }) read what the ACTIVE profile watched and saved in Kino, newest first, one entry per title: { title, year?, kind, ids: { tmdb?, imdb? }, progress (0..1, watched only), watchedAtMs (rounded down to the day, UTC, watched only) }. Never a stream URL, a plugin ref, a library id, a play position in seconds, a profile name, anything of another profile, nor an 18+ title (always left out, even with the 18+ code unlocked). Declarative (no export); needs the person's approval at install and again on the update that adds it, always with the red consent line, the plugin's declared hosts listed beside it; revocable from the plugin's tab in Ajustes (switchLabel), after which every call rejects with permission_denied. Only inside a call the person started from fromFunctions; never in background, prewarm or sync calls. kino.library is an object on every apiVersion 14 runtime: feature-detect with featureDetect. sinceMs is rounded down to the day and compared with each title's rounded time, and progress is rounded to progressStep, so no finer time or position can be probed. 18+ fails closed: a title whose source plugin this device cannot place (uninstalled, only on another device, absent from the catalog) or that has no plugin source is left out. The revoke switch applies to the whole device, every profile, and the person's synced devices. Screen timer ticks (screen.every) count as the person's use while the screen is in front. The consent line, the host list and the switch are the safeguards, not a technical block: a plugin that can fetch can send what it read. Nothing is kept for the plugin: each answer is built per call.

kinoLivePanel.$comment: Task 11, apiVersion 14: the player panel on an En vivo module channel. Kino's own General tab first (generalTabId; the favourite and the channel's brightness, answered by Kino, nothing stored), then the tabs of contributors whose manifest.panel.contributes.kinds holds kind, by the 8k rules (approved, usable, switched on, an 18+ contributor only while unlocked). Contributed tabs show only while the channel on screen was confirmed by its provider's own listing as not 18+, its provider is an installed plugin that is not 18+ and not a reserved provider (own: the person's M3U lists and channels; legacy). The context is exactly contextFields (screen mode adds screenContextAdds); channel is { provider, code, name }; no ref, title, ids, playing, position, duration, paused, seekStepMs, stats or player (notSent). Every player action of a tab on a live channel is dropped whole, logged playerDroppedLog; no playerEvent is sent on live. On a zap every open contributed tab is asked panel(context) again with the new channel (a render, never a press); the panel stays open across zaps. A plugin reads the channel only from the context: there is no kino.player.state().
kinoLivePanel.playerDroppedLog: panel: player actions do nothing on a live channel, dropped (live_channel)

kinoPlayerControl.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "playerControl" (Task 8j), declarative (no export), never on its own. A player action may carry pause (true pauses, false resumes; anything else is dropped); it is a one-shot command, never stored. Each player action has an origin: press, change, submit (the person's, in the panel), refresh (a panel result's own player: its open, a tab, a refreshMs tick, a playerEvent answer's new panel; panel and screen-format results may carry player) and event (a playerEvent answer). Without the capability the plugin whose title plays (the owner) keeps the old rules: every field after a press, change or submit and in a playerEvent answer, except pause, which needs a press; a result's own player never counts. A panel contributed to another plugin's title (manifest.panel.contributes) keeps only seekToMs, only after a press in it. With the capability, approved by the person (consentLine, red, never auto-approved, a kit import starts it unticked) and not switched off (switchLabel, in the plugin's tab in Ajustes, device-wide and synced), every origin counts: the owner keeps every field, a contributed panel keeps contributedWithControl (the stored player properties stay the owner's; its speed is never stored and ends with the title; the person's own speed still wins). An action kept only thanks to the capability is controlled: never while Kino is not in front (the player screen stopped: the background, a Kino page over it), one of Kino's dialogs is up or the person is seeking (heldBy), only pause on a live stream (liveKeeps), at most perMinute in windowMs and one action of any field per minIntervalMs per plugin; and when its origin is not the person's (announcedOrigins) Kino shows a short notice naming the plugin (notice + noticeParts; a name that reads like Kino is qualified), which the plugin cannot word or suppress. Every action, controlled or not, shares one guard: one seek or pause per minIntervalMs per plugin (the panel and its playerEvent calls together). A pause of any origin, the person's press included, is dropped while the phone's player is held for a cast (castingDropsPause: Chromecast or DLNA; never routed to the TV) and when it asks for the state the video is already in (noopPauseDropped: no notice, no budget). A panel nested in an answer (an answer's or a playerEvent answer's panel) carries no player of its own (nestedPanelPlayer false). Without the capability the owner's change, submit and playerEvent actions keep the rules shipped at apiVersion 9 (every field but pause, unheld, unannounced); with it, an owner action that mixes those fields with pause from such an origin becomes wholly controlled. The rules are the same for every plugin and feature: Kino never knows why a plugin asks. Shared cases: plugins/sdk/test/player-control-cases.json.

kinoRoom.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "room" (Task 8l), declarative (no export), never on its own. kino.room is a short-lived mailbox hosted on the person's own device and reached from the Internet through the same Cloudflare quick tunnel Kino opens for "Recibir configuración": no external service, no Kino server. open({ ttlMin?, max?, name?, code?, codeDigits? }) -> { code, words, expiresAtMs } opens the tunnel and the mailbox; the code is codeDigits.default digits unless the plugin asks for codeDigits.min to codeDigits.max (the room's only secret; words are public; see codeDigits for what a short code costs), shown by the plugin, typed or carried by the person; spaces and hyphens are ignored. join({ words, code, name? }) -> { handle, memberId, host: { name }, expiresAtMs }. send(payload, { to?, session? }): payload is a JSON object of at most maxPayloadBytes UTF-8 bytes as the plugin's JSON text and maxPayloadDepth levels deep (the object itself is 1); at most perSecond messages a second, perMinute and bytesPerMinute a minute per member (checked by the sender's Kino and again by the host). The host may send to everyone (to absent or "all") or one memberId; a guest writes to the host (to absent or hostId) or to "all" through the host, never to another member directly. inbox({ since?, limit?, session? }) -> { events: [{ seq, from, kind, payload?, name? }], last, more, reachable }: a bounded mailbox per member (mailboxEvents, mailboxMs), seq only grows, last is the seq to pass as since next time; a guest's inbox asks the host at most every pollIntervalMs and reachable says whether it answered. members({ session? }) -> [{ memberId, name, host }], never an address. close({ session? }); state() -> { role: host|guest|none, joined: [{ handle, memberId, host, expiresAtMs, reachable }], hosted: { code, words, expiresAtMs, members } | null }. Sessions: at most maxJoined joined and maxHosted hosted per device, and at most maxSlotsPerPlugin of them for one plugin (room_busy); session is hostedSession or a joined handle, default the first joined, else the hosted one; a join with the code of a joined session replaces it. open({ code }) is refused unless the plugin is in a room with that code now or opened it itself (a backup endpoint with its own words; the plugin decides who opens one and publishes its words in ordinary messages; failover is the plugin's). Calls: open and join only from openFrom (the person's own action: a screen timer tick or a panel refresh never), send/inbox/members from trafficFrom (ticks included), all with Kino in front; close and state from any live call; never a background call. Every request is sealed (scrypt N=8192 r=8 of the code salted with the words, AES-256-GCM plus HMAC-SHA256, per-member keys, growing sequence, answers bound to their request): a stranger can only guess online, but the code protects against casual access, not against the TLS-terminating tunnel provider targeting a room (it could crack a captured join offline in hundreds of GPU-days (about 400 on average on one high-end GPU) and then read it; no forward secrecy). Requests no member key vouches for share one small budget (429 past it) and never touch a member's; a payload nested past maxPayloadDepth is refused before parsing. A wrong code is refused with nothing keyed; after joinFailuresBeforeLock wrong codes an endpoint refuses joins for lockMs, doubling up to maxLockMs (rate_limited), and after maxFailedJoins wrong codes in its whole life (lockouts included, whoever sends them) it closes itself; Kino tells the person, and the plugin's next calls get room_closed with Kino's userMessage. Members a host has not heard from for idleMs are dropped (leave). The tunnel and the endpoint exist only while a room is open: closed by close(), the TTL, the plugin removed, disabled or switched off (switchLabel, device-wide, synced), the owner's screens switch, Kino in the background for backgroundCloseMinutes (while a room is hosted Android keeps it alive with a foreground service and a visible notification «Sala abierta · N personas» with «Cerrar sala»; Android only), or the app ending. A failure opening the route or reaching a room is room_unreachable with Kino's own userMessage (no internet, a network that blocks it, Cloudflare's rate limit). Payloads are opaque JSON, re-serialised by Kino, never executed, never written to disk. Shared cases: plugins/sdk/test/room-cases.json.

codeDigits.$comment: Task 8w: open({ codeDigits }) asks for a shorter numeric code; join takes any length in range (the host chose it). A short code keeps strangers out only because the words cannot be guessed and the room closes itself after limits.maxFailedJoins wrong codes; whoever captures the traffic and knows the words (the tunnel provider) recovers a 4-digit code offline in milliseconds, so such a room is not private from the provider. The default 12 makes that attack expensive, not impossible.

kinoJobs.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "schedule" (Task 8q): Kino's job scheduler, the kernel of a plugin's background work (owner 2026-10-26: "planificador en la app, tipo cron de Laravel"). The manifest lists jobs (manifest): 1 to maxJobs, each { id (idPattern), label: { es, en? } (1 to labelMaxChars each once control and bidirectional characters are scrubbed), everyMin (one of everyOptions), everyOptions (1 to maxOptions different whole minutes from minEveryMin, WorkManager's floor, to maxEveryMin), runOn? (runOnValues, default runOnDefault; badRunOn otherwise) }; other keys of a job are ignored. The capability and the jobs need each other; the plugin exports job(ctx) with ctx = { id, reason: scheduled|manual, lastRunMs (null before the first run), attempt (1 + the failures in a row) }. The answer is never read (outputIgnored): what the plugin wants kept goes to kino.storage, which its screens read when they open (stale-while-revalidate). Kino shows nothing of a job by itself. A job may use availableApis and read readOnly only: an allow-list, every other API (forbiddenApis and any added later) answers not_allowed (logged), and no UI, screen, panel, go, toast, player control or room can come out of a job (nothing it returns is read). kino.library answers a job only with the plugin's own library approval (the same 18+ rule, rounding and rate); kino.ai.ask (Task 8r) only with its own ai approval, each ask one of the run's maxFetches requests. One run: at most runTimeoutMs; maxFetches requests (the next answers rate_limited), made one at a time; maxResponseBytes of answer bodies, each body read with a cap of what is left (an answer that would cross it is refused with too_large, never handed over); maxStorageWriteBytes written to kino.storage (UTF-8 bytes of keys and values; the next set throws too_large); a cap crossed cuts the run and counts as a failure. A failure is worded by Kino only: network only when kino.fetch itself failed to reach a site in that run. Per plugin at most maxRunsPerDay runs a day (UTC), all its jobs together. A failure waits backoffBaseMin, doubling up to backoffMaxMin, before the next scheduled run; failuresToPause in a row pause the job until the person switches it off and on, or a manual run succeeds. A run never starts while the plugin's own screen, panel or catalog call is in progress (it waits up to foregroundWaitMs, then gives way). Approval: consentLine in red at install and on the update that adds it, never auto-approved, unticked in a kit import; revocable from the plugin's tab in Ajustes (switchLabel, device-wide and synced): off cancels its work at once and refuses even a manual run. Each job starts OFF (opt-in) at everyMin, and OFF again after any gap in its approval on the device (uninstalled, an update without schedule or without that job, a reinstall); an update never makes a switched-on job run more often than before: the person's choice while it is an option, else the nearest option at least as slow as both the new everyMin and the period it ran at; when no option is that slow the job is switched OFF (stamped, so it syncs) and its row asks the person to choose again. Once a run is over (it answered or was cut), every API refuses whatever its evaluation still tries; Kino's own rows in the plugin's tab: the job's switch, its frequency (only everyOptions), "Solo con Wi-Fi" (per plugin, on by default: an unmetered network), the last run and "Ejecutar ahora" (reason manual, the same caps). Works also need a network and the battery not low, and stop with the plugin disabled, removed or updated (a new work then), the job switched off or paused, and the owner's screens kill switch (screensEnabled is the one shared switch for plugin screens, rooms and jobs). fetch keeps the plugin's declared hosts and every fetch rule and quota; sealed values keep their rules. The person's choices (on, frequency, Wi-Fi only) sync between their devices. runOn "any" (the default): each device that has the plugin runs its own job, for its own kino.storage. runOn "preferPhone" (Task 8q-2, owner: the phone does the work and what syncs is the result): ONE of the person's linked devices runs it, and the plugin shares the result with kino.shared (kinoShared). Each device decides by itself from a synced record of the person's devices (election): a device is a candidate when the job is approved, on, not paused and not switched off there, and its last SUCCESSFUL run of the job is within freshPeriods times the job's period (being seen is not enough: a phone whose work never fires, on mobile data with "Solo con Wi-Fi" or force-stopped, loses the job; a time more than maxSkewMs ahead of the reader's clock is not believed); the person's choice whereLabel ("Este aparato" names one device; default: the phone if linked) first, then a candidate phone (the smallest device id), else the smallest id of the others (in practice: the TV that has the plugin runs it itself). A TV never runs it while a fresh phone can. A firing on a device that is not the runner skips at once (no runtime, no network, never a failure) and keeps its work, so the TV takes over when the phone stops (no linked phone, no successful run on the phone for freshPeriods periods, its job paused or switched off there); a rare overlap runs it twice, harmless with last-writer-wins results. "Ejecutar ahora" runs on the device where it is pressed. A plugin may read kino.device ("tv" or "phone", readOnly) to pick a lighter batch on a TV (Kino enforces nothing extra; the job caps apply). Kino's rows for such a job add whereLabel with its two choices and the device that ran it last (lastRunLabel). Task 18 (G2, apiVersion stays 14): kino.seed is among availableApis, under exactly its gate everywhere (sent only while the plugin's telemetry consent is on, cleaned to the anonymous-seed allow-list, capped per process; contract.kinoSeed). A job may say enabledBy (enabledByField): the key of one of the plugin's own toggle settings (else badEnabledBy refuses the manifest, or drops an enhancement's block). That setting, in the profile in use with its default, is the person's on/off for the job: on while the setting is on and the job's row in Ajustes holds no OFF of the person's (the row may still switch it off, and its OFF wins until the person switches the row on again); the setting off is always off. Kino's row says which setting drives it (followsSettingLabel). Everything else is unchanged: the consent line, the schedule switch, the frequency, Solo con Wi-Fi, the caps, the pause after failures, the kill switch.

kinoAi.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "ai" (Task 8r), declarative (no export), never on its own. kino.ai.ask({ prompt, system?, json?, maxChars? }) sends one short text to Kino's text AI (Kilo's free models, the same fixed destination as Kino's own assistant; no key, no server of Kino's) and answers { ok: true, text, model } or { ok: false, error, message }: it never throws (errorCodes; message is Kino's English detail for the author). One-shot: no conversation memory, no streaming, no tools, no images, no files; Kino adds no persona and keeps nothing (logs carry sizes and codes only, never the prompt, the system text or the reply). prompt is a non-empty string of at most maxPromptBytes UTF-8 bytes, system at most maxSystemBytes (too_large past either); maxChars is a whole number from 1 to maxChars (default defaultMaxChars): the reply is cut there. json: true only ASKS the model for JSON (Kino adds jsonInstruction to the system text); the reply comes back as the model wrote it, parseable or not: the plugin parses and validates it (Kino never trusts model output). The model and endpoint are Kino's: the plugin sees only the name of the model that answered (model), never an address, a key or a header. Calls: from fromFunctions only after the person's own action (the same rule as kino.qr.scan: a settings action, a panelAction, or a screenEvent that follows the person's tap or submit; never a screen's open, a timer tick, a load-more, a change, a playerEvent, Home, search or play), and from the plugin's scheduled job (fromJob, Task 8q), where each ask is one of the run's maxFetches requests and is refused once the run is over. Device-wide, over every plugin together: devicePerDay asks a day and deviceMaxInFlight waiting at once (rate_limited past either; the stricter of these and the plugin's own limits applies), so plugins never starve Kino's own assistant, which shares Kilo's anonymous quota. Limits per plugin: perMinute asks in any 60 s (a strict sliding window), perDay a day (UTC; counted on the device), maxInFlight at a time (the next is rate_limited, never queued), timeoutMs to answer, the model list included (timeout; the call's own clock stops meanwhile, a job's does not). A plugin screen's event is still bounded by the session's own 60 s wall clock: ask once per event and batch items into one prompt. unavailable: no model could answer (no internet, every free model busy). refused: anything else (not approved, switched off, the plugin disabled, the owner's switch, the wrong origin, a malformed request). Approval: consentLine in red at install and on the update that adds it, never auto-approved, unticked in a kit import; revocable from the plugin's tab in Ajustes (switchLabel, device-wide and synced): every ask is then refused. What the plugin sends leaves the device: its own UI must tell the person what it sends. The reply is untrusted data written by a model that read text the plugin chose (titles from the web, the person's words): a prompt can be injected into it, so never execute it, never follow instructions found in it, never treat it as markup or as a URL to open without checking it, and validate every field (an id, a category) against what you sent. Kino never shows a reply by itself; the plugin's own screen shows what it decides. Shared cases: plugins/sdk/test/ai-cases.json.
kinoAi.jsonInstruction: Reply with valid JSON only: nothing before or after it, without explanations or code fences.

kinoShared.$comment: apiVersion 14, capability "shared" (Task 8q-2), declarative (no export), never on its own, NOT an approval capability: the consent sheet shows consentLine as a plain line (not red), marked new on the update that adds it (it is the person's own data on the person's own devices, bounded); an update that adds only "shared" applies without a sheet, by design. Per profile: each profile's values sync only as that profile's row, so a TV that carries several people's profiles never hands one person's values to another person's phone; a scheduled job (device-wide) writes to the profile in use. kino.shared.get(key) -> the value or null (never throws for a stored value: one this engine cannot read answers null), and kino.shared.set(key, value) -> true when stored, false when the value was already that one (nothing written, nothing sent); set(key, null) removes the key. Synchronous, like kino.storage; usable from screens, panels, settings and scheduled jobs (on the job allow-list; not bounded by the job's storage budget but by these limits). Values are JSON only: the plugin's JSON.stringify text of any JSON value, at most maxValueBytes UTF-8 bytes, strict JSON (RFC 8259: no leading zeros, no lone . or sign, no empty or trailing elements; checked on write, on arrival and on read) at most maxDepth levels deep, one value; a plugin keeps at most maxKeys keys and maxPluginBytes bytes of values; a key matches keyPattern. Secrets never go here (a value is copied to every linked device): a key is split into words (wordPattern, after splitting at _ . -; lowercased) and refused when a word is one of secretKeyTokens or its plural, or two words in a row make apikey (authToken, api_key, sessions refused; author kept), and so is a value that holds one of the plugin's sealed values or markers; never put tokens, passwords, cookies or sessions in it (keep those in kino.storage or your settings). The values sync between the person's own linked devices, both ways, over the existing sync channel (sealed with each peer's pairing key), last writer wins per key by a clock Kino assigns when the value is written; a key's new value travels at most once per syncEveryMs, and at most tripsPerMinute of a plugin's keys travel in any syncEveryMs (renaming keys gains nothing; the newest value written meanwhile goes; reads on this device see it at once). A plugin keeps at most maxRemovals removals (its own oldest go); a removal is forgotten after tombstoneMs, so a device offline longer may bring an old value back. Never sent anywhere else, never shown, logged or parsed by Kino beyond these checks; removed (on every linked device) when the plugin is removed. Each plugin reaches only its own keys. What a peer sends is checked again on arrival (key, size, depth, strict JSON, caps); past a cap the oldest values are dropped. Treat what get answers as untrusted input: another device wrote it (maybe an older or newer version of your plugin), so validate its shape, sizes and every field before you use it. At most writesPerMinute writes a minute per plugin (rate_limited). Errors (thrown as kino errors): not_allowed (no "shared" capability, the plugin off, a sealed value), bad_request (a key, a value that is not JSON, a secret-like key), too_large (a value, the plugin's keys or bytes), rate_limited. On the wire the store holds at most maxRowEntries keys of all plugins and maxRowBytes of values. A device not linked to any other keeps them as an ordinary local store. Shared cases: plugins/sdk/test/shared-cases.json.

qr.$comment: apiVersion 13. kino.qr.scan({ title?, titleEn? }) (capability qrScan, declarative, no approval): Kino's camera scanner full screen on the phone, under the installed plugin's name, the plugin's title (titleEn in English) and Kino's instruction. Resolves with the decoded text (1 to maxScanChars characters) or null when the person closes it (the close button, Back, leaving the screen, or the call ending). A scan runs only from a settings action, a panelAction or a screenEvent that follows the person's press (fromFunctions: the person pressed one of the plugin's buttons; anything else is not_allowed). Task 8p: a plugin screen's call (a root screen, a screen-mode panel, a contributed tab in screen mode) counts only after the person's own tap or submit (screenTriggers), never its open event, a timer tick (every), a load-more, a change, a panel's refreshMs or a playerEvent. The scanning call's clock is paused while the scanner is up; one scan on screen at a time for the whole app (a second one, from any plugin, is busy). unavailable: this device cannot scan (no camera, or Kino's TV interface). title and titleEn hold no control, bidi or format character (invalid_request); a code over maxScanChars is ignored and the scanner says it is not valid for the plugin. Showing a QR needs no capability: the settings form's qr setting (settingsQr), whose text is settingsStatus()'s answer under its key, asked again when the form opens, after every action and every refreshMs while the form is on screen.

images.$comment: imageSource (apiVersion 13): a poster, backdrop, still or section hero image may be { source: "plugin", handle } instead of a URL; Kino loads it from the plugin's required image({ handle }) export, which answers { bytes: <base64>, mime }. One call in flight per plugin, never while that plugin has an open byte stream or a read queued, running or ended under readQuietMs ago (a timed-out call discards the plugin's runtime: QuickJS cannot be interrupted), kept in the image disk cache per plugin, installed version and handle; a failed handle is left alone for failureTtlMs; pauseAfterTimeouts timeouts in a row pause the plugin's images for pauseMs.
